stories.headline: Czech Republic misses NATO 2% spending target; Babiš and Fiala trade accusations over who is to blame
stories.summary: Prime Minister Babiš announced in a Sunday social-media video that Czech Republic will fall short of the NATO 2% GDP defense-spending pledge in 2026, with NATO recognizing only 1.78% of GDP, and claimed the previous Fiala government also failed to meet the target in 2025. Former PM Fiala and former Defence Minister Černochová immediately pushed back, citing official NATO secretary-general data showing the 2025 target was met, sparking a public dispute that also drew in Speaker Okamura and opposition Pirates leader Hřib.

stories.headline: Government plan to scrap public broadcaster licence fees triggers journalist strike warning and student protests
stories.summary: The Babiš government's proposed media-funding law — which would replace licence fees for Czech Television and Czech Radio with direct state budget transfers — prompted unions at both broadcasters to declare strike readiness, drew thousands of students into street protests, and forced the creation of a government working group including the ČT director-general. Speaker Okamura separately attacked Czech Radio on social media, and the coalition deferred a parliamentary vote on ČT board members amid opposition pressure.

stories.headline: Babiš refuses military plane for Senate chief's Taiwan trip, citing China business ties
stories.summary: Prime Minister Babiš denied Senate President Miloš Vystrčil a government aircraft for a planned business delegation trip to Taiwan, framing the decision as pragmatic foreign policy that should not damage Czech business ties with China; Babiš also offered Vystrčil his personal campaign van in a widely-mocked gesture. The dispute crystallised a broader debate about Czech China policy, with Taiwan's foreign ministry stating Vystrčil remains welcome.

stories.headline: Coalition tensions over Filip Turek's remarks about civil-servant 'parasites'
stories.summary: Coalition government MP and envoy Filip Turek (Motoristé) called civil servants on his ministry 'parasites' and referenced their 'deratisation' at a private event, drawing public condemnation from PM Babiš and Finance Minister Schillerová, and prompting Turek to issue a limited apology. Babiš indicated he plans to discuss the matter directly with Motoristé leader Macinka, and the incident stoked tensions within the governing coalition.

stories.headline: NATO summit delegation dispute: Babiš and President Pavel schedule May 8 talks on who attends Ankara
stories.summary: A public dispute emerged over whether President Pavel or the government delegation led by PM Babiš should represent the Czech Republic at the July NATO summit in Ankara; Babiš said the matter would be resolved after his May 8 meeting with Pavel, which Pavel's office agreed to. Media commentary and a reader poll reflected the constitutional tension between presidential foreign-policy prerogatives and government authority.

stories.headline: KDU-ČSL congress elects Jan Grolich as new party leader; he rules out cooperation with Babiš
stories.summary: At a party congress in Ostrava, the Czech People's Party (KDU-ČSL) elected South Moravian regional governor Jan Grolich as new chairman. Grolich immediately declared that cooperation with Babiš is a 'no-go' and pledged to lead KDU-ČSL into opposition and ultimately government. The congress concluded the cycle of leadership renewals among all three SPOLU parties following their 2025 election defeat.

stories.headline: President Pavel's 'United States of Europe' remarks trigger accusations of treason from Okamura and SPD
stories.summary: President Petr Pavel reiterated at a public event in Litomyšl that European integration into a US-like federal structure may be 'the only solution' for Europe's global relevance, prompting Speaker Okamura and others to accuse him of 'treason' against Czech sovereignty. The controversy generated multiple opinion pieces and a student encounter where Pavel fielded questions about his communist-era past.

stories.headline: Czech Republic summons Russian ambassador over Kremlin threats to Czech defense companies; SPD member accused of blocking ammunition initiative
stories.summary: Czechia and Germany both summoned Russian ambassadors after Russia's Defence Ministry and Dmitry Medvedev published a list of European defense-sector facilities — including Czech firms supporting Ukraine's drone production — as potential military targets. Separately, Deník N reported that an SPD deputy minister of defence had blocked the use of frozen Russian assets for the Czech ammunition initiative, raising conflict-of-interest concerns about pro-Kremlin influence within the coalition.

stories.headline: ČEZ signs Rolls-Royce SMR preparatory deal and advances Korean nuclear partnership
stories.summary: Czech state energy company ČEZ signed an agreement with UK firm Rolls-Royce SMR for preparatory work — including licensing documentation — needed to build the first small modular reactor in the Czech Republic, where ČEZ holds a 20% stake in the British company. Separately, the Czech government said its Dukovany nuclear project with South Korean KEPCO is on schedule with potential for expanded cooperation. Reports also surfaced of plans to spin off ČEZ's distribution, sales and renewable assets into a new subsidiary.

stories.headline: Babiš at EU Cyprus summit: EU budget deal 'extremely difficult,' softening green rules needed
stories.summary: On the margins of an informal EU leaders' summit in Nicosia, PM Babiš told reporters that agreement on the EU's 2028–2034 budget will be 'extremely difficult' and unlikely this year, and criticized the European Commission's spending transparency. He separately called on the EU to loosen environmental rules to ease the impact of energy price spikes from the Iran-related conflict. Babiš also played down Trump's remarks calling NATO a 'paper tiger.'

stories.headline: Czech Republic interested in French nuclear deterrence extension, Babiš says
stories.summary: PM Babiš stated on social media that the Czech Republic should discuss involvement in France's proposed extension of its nuclear deterrence to European allies, triggering criticism from within his own coalition — ANO deputy chairman Vondráček said the US nuclear umbrella is sufficient — and analysis questioning whether the move would require higher defence spending the government has resisted.

stories.headline: Babiš announces new Prague hospital will be military facility; departs for Azerbaijan
stories.summary: PM Babiš announced on X that the planned new hospital in Prague's Letňany district will be built as a military facility with underground floors convertible into a crisis command post, framing it as part of meeting NATO capability commitments. He made the announcement before departing on his first official trip outside the EU — to Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan — during which Czech and Azerbaijani defence ministries signed a bilateral military cooperation plan.

stories.headline: US-NATO tensions and Czech perspectives: Pentagon 'good-and-bad allies' list, Hormuz energy crisis
stories.summary: Leaks of a Pentagon internal email discussing ways to penalise NATO allies who declined to support US operations against Iran — including potentially suspending Spain's membership — generated broad Czech and Slovak commentary about the durability of the alliance. Czech media also covered Dutch intelligence warnings that Russia could be ready to challenge NATO within a year of any Ukraine ceasefire, and the EU Cyprus summit discussed contingency planning for US withdrawal from NATO.

stories.headline: Okamura and SPD in energy security debate: Russian gas versus nuclear; fuel-price regulation law
stories.summary: Speaker Okamura clashed with Piráti leader Hřib on television over Czech energy policy, defending a preference for cheap energy regardless of source — including Russian gas — while opposing renewables. Okamura also outlined government emergency plans to accelerate filling gas reserves amid Hormuz-related energy volatility. A separate parliamentary debate concerned a new fuel-price regulation law enabling faster government intervention in crisis scenarios.

stories.headline: Petr Fiala active in opposition: ODS rebrands on social media, disputes Babiš across multiple issues
stories.summary: Former PM Petr Fiala has become notably more active on social media and in public commentary since leaving office, sparking analysis about whether he is helping or hindering ODS's rebuilding effort; analysts differ on whether his online activity strengthens the opposition or undermines the current ODS chairman. ODS celebrated its 35th anniversary with Fiala, former PMs Topolánek and Nečas present. Fiala also publicly approved of Babiš's decision not to block EU sanctions against Russia.
